why: Arms R2, the per-pass IB circuit breaker. Once ONE IB-routed fetch in an exit-evaluation pass returns a pinned-thread QUEUE timeout, the remaining IB-routed fetches in THAT pass are skipped and their callers get candles=None. IT DECIDES NOTHING: IB market data is serialised on one pinned worker (_IB_FETCH_EXECUTOR, max_workers=1), so while that queue is congested every later fetch in the pass waits its own _IB_FETCH_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_S (29.0s at the shipped default) and returns None ANYWAY -- a skipped package receives exactly the candles=None it would have received 29s later, and order_monitor already short-circuits on it. It bounds the COST of an outcome already determined. EVIDENCE (MEASURED, docs/claude/work/EXIT-EVAL-60S-ROOTCAUSE-2026-09-10.md, a COMPLETE CENSUS of all 1218 within-process breaching intervals read 2026-09-10T06:13Z from /api/bot/exit-interval/soak): every within-process 60s breach is a slow PASS (1218/1218 have pass_ms > 30s; 0 rows have a residual above one cadence period, so no scheduler-stall hypothesis survives), and the live residual is 10 of 14 post-fix breaches inside the 04:00-05:00Z IBKR reset window -- 71.4% against 8.6% for the flat pre-fix population -- where a pass costs n_IB x 29s and crosses 60s at THREE packages. INFERRED from that arithmetic: window pass cost falls from n x 29s to ~35s. THE TRIGGER IS THE QUEUE TIMEOUT, NEVER A BARE None. A gateway outage, an unknown symbol and a venue-side reqHistoricalData timeout all return None and none of them is congestion, so the signal is a THREAD-LOCAL flag raised in get_ohlcv's existing _FutureTimeout branch and read-and-cleared by consume_queue_timeout(). A module counter would also be incremented by the TICK thread, so a pass whose own IB fetch SUCCEEDED could trip -- a widening of what was approved. Read-and-clear so a flag raised in pass N cannot trip pass N+1. Both properties are MUTATION-CHECKED: trip-on-bare-None fails 1 test, hoisting the state out of the per-pass closure fails 4. NON-IB SYMBOLS ARE NEVER SKIPPED -- Bybit does not share the pinned worker, so the real-money path is outside the blast radius. NEITHER TIMEOUT VALUE IS TOUCHED: BL-20260816's own criterion 2 forbids optimising the interval into a MONITOR BLIND. ROLLBACK: EXIT_LOOP_IB_BREAKER_DISABLED truthy, one env flip plus a restart, no redeploy -- the sanctioned EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED shape (a default-OFF kill-switch over an ON capability, NOT a default-off *_ENABLED gate in front of a required one). Only an explicit 1/true/yes/on disarms; a typo leaves it armed. The key is added to get_env.py::ALLOWED_KEYS IN THE SAME CHANGE (the CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S lesson) because an UNSET value IS the armed state, so the only way to establish it is armed on the running trader is to read it off /proc/<MainPID>/environ and see it absent. ATTRIBUTION: the breaker's verdict is stamped onto the EXISTING durable per-pass exit-interval soak row (four never-collapsed states -- no_ib_packages / armed / disabled / absent) rather than into a new soak file, because pass_ms alone cannot tell 'the breaker skipped two packages' from 'the queue was healthy this pass', and the two WARNING lines reach only the systemd journal, whose retention here was measured at ~30 minutes. record_pass's new extra_fields defaults to None and the builder drops None, so every existing caller writes a byte-identical row. TESTS: 27 new, plus the 4 existing exit-loop/monitor modules re-run green (101 total). A GREEN SUITE CLEARS NOTHING HERE -- a harness cannot reach a wedged IB queue; the fleet half is OI-20260910-IB-PER-PASS-BREAKER-ARMED-AND-HAS-SKIPPED-NOTHING. NOT TOUCHED: config/, deploy/, .github/workflows/, any order path, any strategy or risk cap. No order placed, modified or cancelled on any account.
